newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds and futures remain firm, seen supported.
newsitem.headline: Bunds and futures remain firm, seen supported.

text.p: German debt prices were comfortably higher in late trade on Wednesday with traders reporting healthy buying interest from the U.S. in both five and 10-year futures as the dollar faltered against the mark.

Analysts said the market's initial boost, which came from a decision overnight in the U.S. to leave official interest rates steady, was continuing to support Bunds and enouraging U.S. interest in the German market.
While the FOMC left monetary policy steady this time, U.S. players were already looking ahead to the next policy-setting meeting when rate fear will gain take its toll on Treasuries.
"We were pretty aggressive buyers of five and 10-years early in the session -- buying mostly for U.S. customers," said one futures broker in London.
"The dollar is slipping away from them a bit so they are saying 'let's get out of the States and into Europe' -- particularly Germany, Spain and Italy," he added.
By 1400 GMT, the DTB June future was five basis points up at 101.64. June Bobl futures were up 0.07 at 105.11.
Dealers said that as long as dollar setbacks continued to prompt flows out of Treasuries, Bunds should hold up even in the face of a weaker U.S. market.
"Bunds should hold the lows in the 101.60 to 101.70 area," said a trader based in Frankfurt. "Any dip towards those levels should be buying opportunities, at least for the short term."
The June contract traded a range of 101.62 to 101.94 during Wednesday's session, just failing to overcome key upside resistance at 102.00.
In the cash market, the 10-year July 2007 benchmark was quoted at 101.45 by 1403 GMT for a bid yield of 5.800 percent.
The main domestic events will be April M3 money supply, expected in the next few days, and the Ifo business climate index, due for release on Thursday.
Analysts said M3, while expected to slow again, will have little impact for interest rates, but will be Bund-supportive if, as expected, it confirms subdued inflationary pressure.

"M3 growth is still buoyant although it is decelarating somewhat," said Stefan Schneider, an economist at Paribas in Frankfurt. "But so far there is certainly no reason for the Bundesbank to cut interest rates."
The Ifo business index is due at 0800 GMT on Thursday. In March the west German index fell sharply to 92.4 versus 93.6 in February, while the east German index held steady at 104.1.
